newsitem.title: CANADA: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA BLANKS FINLAND 5-0 IN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA BLANKS FINLAND 5-0 IN WORLD CUP.

text.p: Andre Trefilov stopped 27 shots as Russia whitewashed Finland 5-0 Friday to advance to Sunday's semifinal game against the United States in ice hockey's World Cup.

Andrei Nikolishin had a goal and an assist as Russia (2-2) earned a spot against the undefeated United States (3-0) Sunday. The winner will advance to the best-of-three finals against the winner of the Sweden-Canada game Saturday at Philadelphia.

Trefilov, a backup goalkeeper for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League, was making his first start in the World Cup, replacing the Phoenix Coyotes' Nikolai Khabibulin, who had played all three previous games.

Trefilov was particularly sharp during two power-play situations for Finland in the second period when he stopped the Anaheim Mighty Ducks' Teemu Selanne on the doorstep and thwarted the Montreal Canadiens' Saku Koivu twice.
Russian coach Boris Mikhailov said: "Andre Trefilov fullfilled every hope we had for the game. In order to beat a team as skilled and good as Finland the goalie must play well.
"All three of our goalies are very good. The game against the United States will be a tough game."

The Russians, who had lost close games to Canada and the United States and beaten Slovakia, scored first when the New York Rangers' Alexei Kovalev took a cross-the-slot pass from the Ottawa Senators' Alexei Yashin, and steered a 12-foot backhander high into the Finnish net.

At 15:00 of the first period the Washington Capitals' Sergei Gonchar fired a 55-foot point shot past Finnish goalie Jarmo Myllys during a power play to make it 2-0. The Detroit Red Wings' Sergei Fedorov and the Vancouver Canucks' Alexander Mogilny assisted.
Russia got the only goal of the second period when Detroit's Slava Kozlov put Nikolishin of the Hartford Whalers in with a breakaway pass and Nikolishin beat Myllys at 7:36.
Russia picked up two more goals in the final period.

The Toronto Maple Leafs' Dimitri Yushkevich scored at 5:40 on a pass out from Mogilny, who had two assists. The Montreal Canadiens' Andrei Kovalenko made it 5-0 at 6:10, with Nikolishin and Detroit's Igor Larionov assisting.
Trefilov withstood a minute-long two-man Finnish advantage in the final stages of the third period, stopping Ville Peltonen from five feet out. Overall the Finns outshot the Russians 27-20.

Slava Fetisov of the Detroit Red Wings, a Russian team leader, said: "I called a meeting in New York after we lost to the U.S. on Monday and we talked about things like attitude and how were going to play after that. Things could not go on as they were after losing to both Canada and the U.S.
"Sunday against the United States will be a tough game. I don't think they can beat us twice. We know how to play them, we just didn't do it the first time."

Said Finnish coach Curt Lindstrom: "We are disppointed. We lost two big games in a row (to Sweden and Russia). The goalie for Russia played very good. We could not beat him. We got more shots and more chances, but he stopped us."
